1064: theorem update_insertNth (p : Fin (n + 1)) (x y : α p) (f : ∀ i, α (p.succAbove i)) :
1065:     update (p.insertNth x f) p y = p.insertNth y f := by
1066:   simp [eq_insertNth_iff]
1067: 
1068: @[simp]
1069: theorem insertNth_update (p : Fin (n + 1)) (x : α p) (i : Fin n) (y : α (p.succAbove i))
1070:     (f : ∀ j, α (p.succAbove j)) :
1071:     p.insertNth x (update f i y) = update (p.insertNth x f) (p.succAbove i) y := by
1072:   simp [insertNth_eq_iff]
1073: 
1074: /-- Equivalence between tuples of length `n + 1` and pairs of an element and a tuple of length `n`
1075: given by separating out the `p`-th element of the tuple.
1076: 
1077: This is `Fin.insertNth` as an `Equiv`. -/
1078: @[simps symm_apply]
1079: def insertNthEquiv (α : Fin (n + 1) → Type u) (p : Fin (n + 1)) :
1080:     α p × (∀ i, α (p.succAbove i)) ≃ ∀ i, α i where
1081:   toFun f := insertNth p f.1 f.2
1082:   invFun f := (f p, removeNth p f)
1083:   left_inv f := by ext <;> simp
1084:   right_inv f := by simp
1085: 
1086: /- `@[simps]` over-applies, while `@[simps -fullyApplied]` under-applies, so this is manually
1087: written. -/
1088: @[simp]
1089: theorem insertNthEquiv_apply (α : Fin (n + 1) → Type*) (p : Fin (n + 1))
1090:     (f : α p × ∀ i, α (p.succAbove i)) :
1091:     insertNthEquiv α p f = insertNth p f.1 f.2 :=
1092:   rfl
1093: 
1094: @[simp] lemma insertNthEquiv_zero (α : Fin (n + 1) → Type*) : insertNthEquiv α 0 = consEquiv α :=
1095:   Equiv.symm_bijective.injective <| by ext <;> rfl
1096: 
1097: /-- Note this lemma can only be written about non-dependent tuples as `insertNth (last n) = snoc` is
1098: not a definitional equality. -/
1099: @[simp] lemma insertNthEquiv_last (n : ℕ) (α : Type*) :
1100:     insertNthEquiv (fun _ ↦ α) (last n) = snocEquiv (fun _ ↦ α) := by ext; simp

1102: /-- A `HEq` version of `Fin.removeNth_removeNth_eq_swap`. -/
1103: theorem removeNth_removeNth_heq_swap {α : Fin (n + 2) → Sort*} (m : ∀ i, α i)
1104:     (i : Fin (n + 1)) (j : Fin (n + 2)) :
1105:     i.removeNth (j.removeNth m) ≍
1106:       (i.predAbove j).removeNth ((j.succAbove i).removeNth m) := by
1107:   apply Function.hfunext rfl
1108:   simp only [heq_iff_eq]
1109:   rintro k _ rfl
1110:   unfold removeNth
1111:   apply congr_arg_heq
1112:   rw [succAbove_succAbove_succAbove_predAbove]
1113: 
1114: /-- Given an `(n + 2)`-tuple `m` and two indexes `i : Fin (n + 1)` and `j : Fin (n + 2)`,
1115: one can remove `j`th element from `m`, then remove `i`th element from the result,
1116: or one can remove `(j.succAbove i)`th element from `m`,
1117: then remove `(i.predAbove j)`th element from the result.
1118: 
1119: These two operations correspond to removing the same two elements in a different order,
1120: so they result in the same `n`-tuple. -/
1121: theorem removeNth_removeNth_eq_swap {α : Sort*} (m : Fin (n + 2) → α)
1122:     (i : Fin (n + 1)) (j : Fin (n + 2)) :
1123:     i.removeNth (j.removeNth m) = (i.predAbove j).removeNth ((j.succAbove i).removeNth m) :=
1124:   heq_iff_eq.mp (removeNth_removeNth_heq_swap m i j)
1125: 
1126: end InsertNth

1128: section Find
1129: 
1130: variable {p q : Fin n → Prop} [DecidablePred p] [DecidablePred q] {i j : Fin n}
1131: 
1132: private def findX {n : ℕ} (p : Fin n → Prop) [DecidablePred p] (h : ∃ k, p k) :
1133:     { i : Fin n // p i ∧ ∀ j < i, ¬ p j } := go n (by grind) where
1134:   go (m : Nat) (hj : ∀ j (hm : j < n - m), ¬p ⟨j, by grind⟩) := match m with
1135:   | m + 1 => if hnm : p ⟨_, n.sub_lt h.choose.pos (by grind)⟩
1136:     then ⟨_, ⟨hnm, (hj ·.val)⟩⟩ else go m (by grind)
1137:   | 0 => absurd h (fun ⟨⟨_, _⟩, _⟩ => by grind)
1138: 
1139: /-- `Fin.find p h` returns the smallest index `k : Fin n` where `p k` is satisfied,
1140:   given that it is satisfied for some `k`. -/
1141: @[no_expose]
1142: protected def find {n : ℕ} (p : Fin n → Prop) [DecidablePred p] (h : ∃ k, p k) : Fin n :=
1143:   (Fin.findX p h).1
